solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Summary is not quite accurate

indicators.note: not quite means the word for accurate falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: accurate means precise

explanation.surface: A complaint that some abstract or digest gets the facts slightly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the last letter E from PRECISE.
explanation.definitionFit: A précis is a short written abstract giving the gist of a longer text.

clue.text: PM's diary sets out high points of NE African tour

definitions.text: high points of NE African tour

indicators.note: sets out means the letters are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister's diary plans the highlights of a trip to Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sets out' rearranges PMSDIARY.
explanation.definitionFit: The great tombs at Giza are the tall peaks, and highlights, of a tour of Egypt.

clue.text: Cries on seeing awful climaxes

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters are badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone cries out at dreadful endings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges CLIMAXES.
explanation.definitionFit: To call out loudly in surprise or emotion is to cry out.

clue.text: Risk including a kind of measure

indicators.note: including means the risk word takes the letter a inside it

parts.note: to imperil is to risk or endanger

explanation.surface: A gamble that involves some sort of measurement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts A inside IMPERIL.
explanation.definitionFit: The imperial system is the British set of units such as feet, pints and pounds.

clue.text: Something helpful that may get you into Oxford

definitions.text: Something helpful that may get you into Oxford

parts.words: Something helpful that may get you into Oxford
parts.note: reads like help with university entry, but an Oxford is a style of laced shoe, and this tool eases a foot into it

explanation.surface: Advice on gaining a place at Oxford University.
explanation.walkthrough: An Oxford is a laced leather shoe; the curved tool helps your heel slide into it.
explanation.definitionFit: The curved tool slips into the heel of footwear so the foot can be eased inside it.

clue.text: Saw distress in her cable

indicators.note: in places the scrambled word inside the letters of her
distress means the word saw is battered into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone saw a woman in trouble tangled in a cable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distress' looks like the woman's plight but signals the anagram; 'in' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawser is a thick rope or cable used for mooring or towing a ship.

clue.text: Not the genuine article from bankers at Zurich

indicators.note: from means the letters are drawn from within the words bankers at Zurich

explanation.surface: Counterfeit goods coming from the gnomes of Zurich.
explanation.walkthrough: Swiss bankers are famous, so the surface feels natural.
explanation.definitionFit: An ersatz thing is an inferior substitute or imitation, not the real product.

clue.text: Possibly tore in from the East

indicators.note: Possibly suggests the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone may have stormed in from eastern lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges TORE IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient is a literary name for the countries of Asia, lying eastward of Europe.

clue.text: Almost a point too soon

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass
early means before the expected time

explanation.surface: Scoring almost a point, but too early.
explanation.walkthrough: N is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean all but, very close to completion.

clue.text: Kitchener's formula for success?

parts.note: suggests Lord Kitchener's military plan, but a kitchener is simply someone working in a kitchen, whose formula is a set of cooking instructions

explanation.surface: Asks how the famous British field marshal Lord Kitchener won his campaigns.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Kitchener was a British field marshal; read 'Kitchener' as a cook in a kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook follows written instructions listing ingredients and method to produce a successful dish.

clue.text: Many Nazis were armed with this

definitions.text: Many Nazis were armed with this

parts.words: Many Nazis were armed with this
parts.note: armed looks like carrying weapons, but here it means wearing something on the arm, as an armband

explanation.surface: A statement about the weapons carried by Nazi soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'armed' means wearing it on the arm: Nazi party members wore armbands bearing the hooked cross.
explanation.definitionFit: The hooked cross emblem appeared on the armbands worn by Nazi party members.

clue.text: Many agree it's new and in short supply

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

indicators.note: new tells us the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A crowd concurs that something novel is scarce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges M plus AGREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scanty or lacking in quantity is said to be meagre.

clue.text: Guard dispatched one with a half-nelson

parts.note: dispatched means sent off
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: half signals taking the first half of the word nelson

explanation.surface: A wrestling bout: the guard was sent off after using a half-nelson hold.
explanation.walkthrough: A half-nelson is a wrestling hold; here 'half' takes the first three letters of NELSON.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentinel is a sentry or watchman posted to keep watch.

clue.text: A land is devastated by ancient Muslim warrior

indicators.note: devastated means the words are laid waste and reassembled

explanation.surface: A country is laid waste by an old Islamic fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is devastated' rearranges A LAND IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Saladin was the twelfth-century sultan who fought the Crusaders and took Jerusalem.

clue.text: Pitch of the road

parts.note: pitch suggests slope or gradient, but here it is the black sticky substance used to surface roads

explanation.surface: Sounds like the slope of a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' is the dark sticky substance, not a gradient.
explanation.definitionFit: Road surfaces are laid with a black bituminous substance, another name for pitch.

clue.text: Humble cleric takes me in

indicators.note: the cleric takes the word me inside it, holding it within
in confirms the word me goes within the cleric's title

parts.note: a dean is a senior cleric of a cathedral

explanation.surface: A modest churchman offers me shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humble' reads as an adjective describing the cleric, but it is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To humble someone is to lower their dignity, to degrade or belittle them.

clue.text: Get neither number right

explanation.surface: Getting no answer correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neither ... nor' are paired words, so one stands for the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The pair of negatives go together, so one partner word can clue the other in crosswords.

clue.text: For the returning traveller

indicators.note: returning means the word for traveller is read backwards

parts.note: a rep, a sales representative, is a commercial traveller

explanation.surface: Something intended for someone coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns REP around.
explanation.definitionFit: Per means for each, as in a price per head.

clue.text: Places drawn roughly to scale

indicators.note: something drawn roughly is sketched loosely, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A map where the places are sketched approximately to scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn roughly' rearranges TO SCALE. 'Places' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To place something is to position or find it, as one finds a spot on a map.

clue.text: Examination on this writer I don't know

parts.note: a search is a close examination
this writer is the setter, so me

explanation.surface: A writer being examined pleads ignorance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this writer' is the setter referring to themself.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial phrase is a shrugging reply admitting one has no idea.

clue.text: Guard the stupid girl

indicators.note: stupid suggests the words are muddled into nonsense, then reordered

explanation.surface: A command to protect a foolish young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupid' rearranges GUARD THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter is a female child, so a girl.

clue.text: He's crazy to pocket ball at end of break

indicators.note: at end of places the snooker word after the word for break

parts.note: to crack is to break
in snooker or pool, to pot is to pocket a ball

explanation.surface: Snooker talk: a player is mad to sink a ball at the end of a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' is a snooker term too, adding to the misdirection; POT goes at the end of CRACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackpot is an eccentric or deranged person, a crank.

clue.text: Go about two

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a pair is two

explanation.surface: A terse instruction to two people to move around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' as in 'repair to the drawing room'.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair to a place, in formal usage, means to go there.

clue.text: It's not just perfume that's upset and left

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: an aroma is a scent or perfume

explanation.surface: Someone is upset by more than perfume, and walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns AROMA into AMORA in this down clue. 'just' means fair, not merely.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without moral principles is not righteous or fair.

clue.text: The whole country is full of conservationists

indicators.note: is full of puts the conservation body inside the country

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage and conservation charity

explanation.surface: An entire nation teeming with environmentalists.
explanation.walkthrough: NT is the National Trust, the British charity that conserves historic buildings and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire means whole, complete, with nothing missing.

clue.text: False alibi initially excluded by Scottish magistrate

indicators.note: False suggests the letters are faked into a different order
initially takes the first letter of the word excluded

explanation.surface: A Scottish judge throws out a bogus alibi at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'False' rearranges ALIBI plus E, the first letter of 'excluded'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bailie is a municipal magistrate or alderman in Scotland.

clue.text: A bird that is after quiet

indicators.note: after places the abbreviation for that is behind the letter for quiet

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: Describing a bird that comes along once things are silent.
explanation.walkthrough: Pie is an old name for the magpie.
explanation.definitionFit: The magpie was formerly called simply a pie, a name kept in crosswords.

clue.text: I creep around and force a way in

indicators.note: around means the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A burglar creeping about and breaking in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges I CREEP.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce is to puncture or penetrate, making a way through.

clue.text: Chinese fruit

definitions.meaning: a Chinese official, or the standard language of China
a small citrus fruit like a tangerine

explanation.surface: Looks like a menu item: a Chinese fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a Chinese official or language and a loose-skinned orange.

clue.text: Unfortunate soldier trapped in reversing vehicle

indicators.note: trapped in puts the soldier inside the vehicle
reversing means the vehicle's word is read backwards

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier pinned by a reversing truck: an unlucky accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' makes the vehicle TRAC, which then has the soldier 'trapped in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something calamitous or disastrous is tragic, a stronger kind of unlucky.

clue.text: Mocking bird with tips of tail blue or grey

parts.note: a rail is a wading bird, such as the water rail

indicators.note: tips of here means the end letters of each following word

explanation.surface: Describes a bird with a blue or grey tail that mocks, like a mockingbird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips of' takes the last letters L, E, R, Y of 'tail blue or grey'.
explanation.definitionFit: Raillery is good-humoured teasing or banter, mocking used as a noun.

clue.text: Reduced to silence when imprisoned

definitions.meaning: made to stop talking, as when told to be quiet

explanation.surface: A prisoner silenced once locked away.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both silenced and locked away or confined.

clue.text: Chap from Belgium is a loyal subject

definitions.meaning: a man from Liège, a city in eastern Belgium
a vassal sworn to serve his feudal lord

explanation.surface: A Belgian fellow proves a faithful subject.
explanation.walkthrough: Both definitions are singular while the grid's entry is plural; the setter slipped, and the crossing letters confirm the plural form.
explanation.definitionFit: Feudal vassals bound to serve a lord, read also as men of the Belgian city of Liège.

clue.text: From around the globe I ruthlessly acquire capital

indicators.note: From around means the letters are taken from within the words around them

explanation.surface: A ruthless collector acquires wealth from all over the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money; it is a capital city, Lebanon's.
explanation.definitionFit: Beirut is the capital city of Lebanon.
